source.rationale: F, retuned 2026-08-25 to the WINDOWED page. The probe now always sends a delivery-date window (the parser's bounds, else the injected last-90-days default), and ANY date filter lifts the CRM's external top-20 cap (_EXTERNAL_ORDERS_LIST_LIMIT_CAP, orders.py:22) to the full window, hard-limited at _EXTERNAL_ORDERS_DATE_SCOPED_LIMIT = 1000 (orders.py:41,60-61; the route itself allows no more, limit le=1000 at orders.py:291, and the MCP layer slims fields but cuts no rows, server.py _slim_orders_list_response). Nothing in the envelope reports truncation, so a page that arrives AT 1000 is still the only signal that rows were cut, and the same asymmetry holds: a candidate whose rows fell off the page would read '- no delivery in the last 90 days' on evidence that was never gathered. All 1000 rows here belong to A CRAFT IDEA - the windowed restatement of the measured exec 13863242 shape (one family filled the whole unwindowed 20-page) - so the other two candidates were possibly never reached and the node must suppress every suffix, render the bare picker byte-identical to gate_clarification, and report page_saturated. Note it withholds the suffix from A CRAFT IDEA too, even though that one IS proven: a page half measured and half guessed is the asymmetry the suppress-all rule exists to avoid. The 20-row single-family page that used to trip this guard now annotates instead - that case moved to exec13863242.json, which is the whole point of the retune: the guard now keys on the lifted in-window limit, not on the unwindowed top-20 cap the probe no longer runs under.
